You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Copenhagen „Nyhavn“ (New Harbor) is famous for its houses with colorful gables built along the waterside. The players face the challenge of constructing new facades in a way that fits perfectly in with this picturesque harbor scenery. The goal of the game is to be the first player to score 12 or more points, or to have the most points when the End of Game card is revealed. Players will collect cards of different colors from the display, which they can use to purchase facade tiles of the same color in different shapes and sizes. Players will use these tiles to construct the facade of their house little by little. Each time a floor (row) is completed they will score 1 point, and 2 points for finishing a section of the house (column). However, these points are doubled if the row or column is made entirely of windows. When players cover one of the coats of arms, or finish a floor with a coat of arms, they will gain a special ability which will help them reach their goal faster. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Player Turn 2.1 Taking Cards 2.2 Constructing Facade 2.2.1 Discarding cards 2.2.2 Placing the tile 3 Getting and using ability tiles (Coat of Arms) 3.1 How to activate Coat of Arms symbols 3.2 Activation Actions 3.2.1 Take a Special Tile 3.2.2 Take a New Ability Tile 3.2.3 Re-activate All Their Ability Tiles 4 Ability Tiles 4.1 Any Cards 4.2 Additional Card 4.3 Construction Discount 4.4 Change of Colors 4.5 Both Actions 5 End of Game 5.1 End of Game Card Goal Be the first player to score 12 points (or, if no one has reached 12 points by the time the "End of Game" card is revealed, be the player with the most points). Players score points by completing complete lines on their board, and points are doubled if the line is composed entirely of window spaces. Specifically, points are scored in the following ways: Completing a horizontal row (or "floor") = +1 point If all squares of the row have windows, score 1 additional point (for a total of +2 points). Completing a vertical column (or "section") = +2 points If all squares of the column have windows, score 2 additional points (for a total of +4 points). Player Turn On their turn, each player may do ONE of the following: Take cards Construct facade Taking Cards If a player chooses to take cards, they MUST take 1 card of the 7 available, as well as 1 more card that is immediately adjacent to the first. The row of available cards does NOT "wrap around" (i.e., the last card in the row is NOT adjacent to the first). Empty spaces are not filled with new cards until the end of a player's turn. After drawing, the player must discard down to the hand limit, which is 7 cards. Constructing Facade This option consists of placing a tile from the supply (by discarding cards equal to its cost) as follows: Discarding cards To buy a tile, a player must first discard one card of that tile's color for each window/brick square on the tile. Note if this new tile touches another tile of the same color when placed, the player may discard 1 less card to pay for it. Placing the tile They then place the tile on a "supported" area of their player board. At least one space on the new tile must be directly above the bottom of the player board, or a space on an existing tile Note the laws of physics need not apply here -- the piece does NOT need to "balance" on top of its supporting facade tile, it just has to be supported below at least one space of the new tile. Getting and using ability tiles (Coat of Arms) Ability Tiles allow players to bend the rules when gaining cards and placing tiles. The way to use (and reuse) these ability tiles is through activating Coat of Arms. How to activate Coat of Arms symbols Each player board has 7 Coat of Arms spaces printed on it: 4 on specific spaces on the board, plus 3 more next to the highlighted rows (outside legal tile placement). [Rating: 1/10] Taking the TTR mechanism of making a set of the same coloured cards, and then take away what's left of the player interaction in TTR with tetris on your own player board.

[Rating: 1/10] Polyomino game combined with TtR style card sets.  But the interaction is super low.

[Rating: 1/10] Shameless publisher, no after sale service at all. Please avoid buying game from them.

[Rating: 1/10] This seems like a bunch of parts stolen from other games and frankensteined together, with individual parts stitched together randomly, so that this atrocity, quickly after being awakened, having no balance, topples over again, bits and pieces flying everywhere. What were they thinking.... oh... yeah... not.

[Rating: 3/10] This was a real let down. I was already hesitant in thinking I might not like it, and it still undershot my already downgraded expectations. There is just nothing interesting about this game. Trivial draft, polyominos, no fun scoring, abilities that are discounts and extra actions. Y'all phoned it in on this one.

[Rating: 3/10] One of the most derivative games I have every played. Lack of real choice and luck of the draw make this an uninteresting, boring affair.

[Rating: 4/10] Ticket to Ride combined with Tetris. Seemed like a cool idea, but turned out to be really boring to play.

[Rating: 4/10] Surprisingly dull and contentless game. I would have expected to like this as I usually have liked polyomino games, but this is totally too simple and too repetitive for my tastes.

[Rating: 4/10] Very decent game. Doesn't overstay it's welcome. Only sad part is that it just doesn't really stand out from the crowd of similar lightweight games.
